newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Police step up search in Belgian sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Police step up search in Belgian sex scandal.

text.p: Belgian police searched an old mine shaft on Saturday for new evidence in the country's paedophile kidnapping, sex abuse and murder scandal in which four girls have been found dead.

Witnesses said dozens of police had arrived near the shaft in the Jumet suburb of the southern city of Charleroi, just 4 km (2.5 miles) from a house owned by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, chief suspect in the case.
Last month, police found the decomposed bodies of teenagers An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks in the garden of the house.
It was formerly occupied by Dutroux accomplice Frenchman Bernard Weinstein. Dutroux admits murdering him and blames him for killing the two girls.

Belgian media said Dutroux and his wife Michele Martin had led police to the shaft on Friday and told them where to look for evidence. The two had lived temporarily in a caravan near the shaft, media said.

In August, Dutroux had led police to the bodies of two eight-year-old children and that of Weinstein at another house owned by Dutroux near Charleroi. Dutroux said the two children, Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo, starved to death earlier this year, some nine months after being abducted.
Two other girls, Laetitia Delhez and Sabine Dardenne, were rescued from another of Dutroux's houses in August.
Several other Belgian girls have gone missing in recent years. Their files are all now pooled in Neufchateau, nerve centre of the international paedophile investigation.
The discovery of the web has stunned Europe, prompted the Belgium to tighten rules on early release of sex offenders and triggered calls for a global war against child sex trade.
